Claim 26 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are drawn when the document is displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order, wherein the first value is calculated based on a spatial relationship between the first and second primitive graphic elements that includes at least one of: a distance between the elements, a relative position of the elements, or an overlap characteristic of the elements; and based on the comparison of the first value to other values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements, wherein the defining step comprises determining that the first and second primitive graphic elements share a common visual or functional purpose based on the spatial relationship.

Claim 27 (Previously presented): (Original)

Claim 28 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value represents a size of a smallest bounding box that encompasses the first and second primitive graphic elements, and wherein the size is calculated as a normalized ratio relative to a page dimension.

Claim 29 (Previously presented): (Original)

Claim 30 (Previously presented): (Original)

Claim 31 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the set of instructions for calculating comprises a set of instructions for calculating a different value for each pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order based on a specific spatial metric, wherein the set of instructions for defining the single structural graphic element comprises sets of instructions for: using the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements through a multi-stage filtering process; identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect and whose spatial relationship satisfies a threshold criterion; and joining the sequences as single graphic elements only when the threshold criterion is met.

Claim 32 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements using a specific calculation method that considers spatial proximity and geometric characteristics, defining a set of successive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element; using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set through an iterative intersection-based algorithm; and defining each particular subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a single structural graphic element within the document, the structure graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the particular subset, wherein the structural graphic element is formed only when the subset elements exhibit a predetermined spatial coherence measure.

Claim 33 (Previously presented): (Original)

Claim 34 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements comprises sets of instructions for: selecting a first graphic element in the cluster and assigning the graphic element to a new sub-cluster; assigning a second graphic element in the cluster to the sub-cluster when a bounding box of the second graphic element overlaps a bounding box of the sub-cluster by at least a minimum overlap threshold; wherein the minimum overlap threshold is determined based on a predefined spatial coherence criterion.
